status_evidence.provider: Cached Nasdaq national trading and SSR status

method: Historical listing-venue quotes at 1 and 30 seconds after the open; cover quotes one second before the scheduled close, including early closes. Use records available by each decision time, at most 30 seconds old. Require completed MBP events and reject provider bad-timestamp/book-gap flags. Bid for selling, ask for covering. Depth study sweeps up to ten displayed levels for the original position sizes. No daily-range proxy or tick-floor substitute.
limits: Listing-venue quotes are not consolidated NBBO and may show wider spreads than a smart router can access.

The multi-venue sensitivity combines available books among the listing venue, NYSE Arca and Cboe EDGX; it can fall back to a single valid venue. Counts of pairs with multiple venues at both times are reported. This is a subset of venues, not full NBBO, and assumes access to their displayed liquidity.

Displayed quotes and depth estimate instantaneous execution costs; they do not establish broker fills, queue outcomes, latency or dynamic market impact. Account comparisons also require affirmative cached Nasdaq trading status at both times and unrestricted SSR at entry. Venue-specific order and auction eligibility still require review.
Sampled BBO is rounded to one-second boundaries. Event-level MBP-10 is used for the account study.
Continuous trading near the auctions uses different prices and times from actual auction participation. Timing differences are reported separately from spread and book depth.

Comparisons preserve the old entry selection and share sizes, use a full same-session cover where displayed depth fits, and retain assumed borrowing. The previous volume-cap model delayed part of six covers; its different exit-path P&L is recorded separately. This study does not replay margin or prove an approved locate.
Missing exit books and insufficient exit depth remain disclosed. Complete-pair subsets are not a full-account net-profit estimate.
Additional 5/10/25bp slippage per side is an uncalibrated latency/impact sensitivity; zero-extra-cost estimates only the displayed static book.

Latency diagnostics compare displayed execution-price changes after 10/100/500ms, using the same quantities on both legs. They measure market movement without our orders and do not estimate our causal market impact, broker latency distribution or guaranteed delayed fills.

definitions.gross: Shares × entry midpoint for quote scenarios; opening auction price for descriptive price cohorts. Gross exposure counts one side, not entry-plus-exit turnover.
definitions.margin: Equity required, excluding encumbered short-sale proceeds. Greater of 50% of market exposure, FINRA per-share maintenance floors and the selected house fraction. Historical broker-specific requirements are not supplied.
definitions.aggregation: Account scenario returns divide summed P&L by summed entry exposure or margin. Capital is reused across dates: this is not a portfolio annual return or P&L divided by peak capital. Peak simultaneous entry capital is shown separately.
definitions.costs: Cost fractions are positive amounts consumed. Subtract spread, depth, timing changes, borrow and commissions from gross price P&L; timing can be negative.
definitions.tail: Historical VaR is a sample loss percentile; expected shortfall is the average of the worst ceil(5% × n) observations. 99% estimates require at least 100 observations. Stress scenarios have no assigned probability.
definitions.intraday: Listing-venue regular-session minute highs. Full entry/exit minute extremes are conservative bounds and can fall just outside the actual position window. Interior-minute results omit those boundary minutes. Prices are marks, not observed size-adjusted cover fills.

matched_controls_on_margin.basis: Same paired observations; equal gross notional within each matched control basket; return divided by its modeled entry margin. Missing margin price bases are excluded and counted.

limits: Observed tails are conditional on available data and repeated issuers. Small execution samples do not establish rare-event probabilities.
A planned one-day hold does not bound losses if liquidity vanishes, a recall forces a buy-in or the broker raises requirements.
Short losses have no finite upper bound. The largest +500% scenario is an illustration, not a worst possible outcome.
Stress cash budget adds potential cover loss, costs and stressed margin as a conservative reserve; those obligations do not all settle at the same instant.
The three-largest-position stress is a hypothetical correlated basket; it does not claim those positions historically overlapped.
The fixed-position daily path assumes same-day covers and no resizing, cash interest or new admissions after costs change. It is not the full production account replay.
